## Overview

`fit` maximises the exact likelihood over the parameters of a rate model.
Here the birth rate is continuous piecewise linear with knots at $0$, $T/2$ and $T$,
and the death rate is constant (its three knots are tied by a `Constraints` equality group).
Ages are drawn from the exact age laws with `simulate_ages_from_rates`,
so the only error is statistical.

From survivor ages alone the early-time rates are weakly identified:
the population size fixes only $\pi(T)$, and the ages separate the rest slowly.
So the knots that matter most for the ages (middle and end) are recovered well,
while the first knot and the death rate trade off.
This is a property of the data, not of the optimiser.

## Setup

```{python}
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

import altair as alt
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from bdpinf import find_project_root
from bdpinf.inference import (
    AgeData,
    BirthDeathModel,
    Constraints,
    fit,
    profile_likelihood_interval,
)
from bdpinf.models.rate_functions import PiecewiseConstantRate, PiecewiseLinearRate
from bdpinf.simulation import simulate_ages_from_rates
from bdpinf.visualization import save_chart
from bdpinf.visualization.altair_theme import PTOLQUAL

figures_dir = find_project_root() / "figures" / "validation" / "time_varying_rates"
figures_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

## Simulate and fit

```{python}
horizon = 6.0
epoch_end_times = [horizon / 2, horizon]
true_birth_knots = np.array([1.0, 1.8, 0.9])
true_death = 0.4

times = jnp.array(epoch_end_times)
true_birth = PiecewiseLinearRate.continuous(jnp.array(true_birth_knots), times)
true_death_rate = PiecewiseConstantRate(jnp.array([true_death, true_death]), times)

model = BirthDeathModel.piecewise_linear(epoch_end_times)
constant_death = Constraints(equal=[model.death_names])

n_replicates = 30
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
rows = []
fits = []
for replicate in range(n_replicates):
    sample = simulate_ages_from_rates(true_birth, true_death_rate, rng)
    data = AgeData.from_groups([sample.all_ages], horizon, is_ordered=True)
    result = fit(data, model, constraints=constant_death)
    fits.append((data, result))
    rows.append(
        {
            "replicate": replicate,
            "population": sample.population,
            "converged": result.converged,
            "interior": result.at_interior_optimum,
            **{name: result.params[name] for name in model.birth_names},
            "death": result.params["death.knot0"],
            "log_likelihood": result.log_likelihood,
        }
    )
fit_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(fit_df.describe().loc[["count", "mean", "50%", "std"]].round(3).to_string())
```

## Recovery of the birth knots

```{python}
long = fit_df.melt(
    id_vars=["replicate", "population"],
    value_vars=[*model.birth_names, "death"],
    var_name="parameter",
    value_name="estimate",
)
truth = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "parameter": [*model.birth_names, "death"],
        "truth": [*true_birth_knots, true_death],
    }
)
points = (
    alt.Chart(long)
    .mark_circle(opacity=0.6, size=40, color=PTOLQUAL[0])
    .encode(
        x=alt.X("parameter:N", title=None, sort=None),
        y=alt.Y("estimate:Q", title="Estimate", scale=alt.Scale(type="symlog")),
    )
)
marks = (
    alt.Chart(truth)
    .mark_tick(color=PTOLQUAL[1], thickness=3, size=40)
    .encode(x=alt.X("parameter:N", sort=None), y="truth:Q")
)
fig_recovery = (points + marks).properties(
    width=420, height=300, title="Estimates (dots) against truth (ticks)"
)
save_chart(fig_recovery, "vtv03_piecewise_linear_recovery", output_dir=figures_dir)
fig_recovery
```

## Nesting: constant rates inside piecewise linear

A flexible model can never fit worse than a model it contains.
Check the likelihood of the constant-rate special case against the linear fit on every replicate.

```{python}
constant_model = BirthDeathModel.piecewise_constant([horizon])
gaps = []
for data, result in fits:
    constant = fit(data, constant_model, compute_covariance=False)
    gaps.append(result.log_likelihood - constant.log_likelihood)
print(f"minimum log-likelihood gain over constant rates: {min(gaps):.2e}")
print(f"median gain: {float(np.median(gaps)):.3f}")
assert min(gaps) > -1e-6
```

## A profile-likelihood interval

Wald intervals are not asymptotically valid for growth-type parameters,
so use the profile likelihood for the end knot of the birth rate on one replicate.

```{python}
data, result = fits[0]
low, high = profile_likelihood_interval(result, data, "birth.knot2")
wald_low, wald_high = result.confidence_intervals()["birth.knot2"]
print(
    f"estimate        {result.params['birth.knot2']:.3f} (true {true_birth_knots[2]})"
)
print(f"profile 95% CI  [{low:.3f}, {high:.3f}]")
print(f"Wald 95% CI     [{wald_low:.3f}, {wald_high:.3f}]")
```
